_about: Canned model outputs run through chat.check_answer on the real data. Placeholders: [{ref:ID}] is the citation ref the question assigns to record ID; {score:ID} is that gene's Open Targets PCOS score. 'accept' answers are faithful paraphrases a good model would write; 'reject' answers are the ways a model goes wrong.

accept.a: Flutamide is a nonsteroidal antiandrogen that binds the androgen receptor and blocks the action of testosterone [{ref:therapeutic-flutamide}]. Its curated target is AR [{ref:gene-ar}].
Letrozole is a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor that blocks CYP19A1 [{ref:therapeutic-letrozole}]. CYP19A1 is its curated target [{ref:therapeutic-letrozole}].

Pioglitazone is a selective agonist of PPARγ [{ref:therapeutic-pioglitazone}]. It increases transcription of insulin-responsive genes and enhances tissue sensitivity to insulin [{ref:therapeutic-pioglitazone}].

accept.q: how does the leptin receptor relate to PCOS
accept.a: LEPR encodes the leptin receptor [{ref:gene-lepr}]. Its Open Targets association score with PCOS is {score:gene-lepr} [{ref:gene-lepr}].
PCOS, also known as PMOS, is an endocrine-metabolic-ovarian condition that this knowledge base integrates evidence around [{ref:process-pcos}].

Androgen biosynthesis is a Reactome pathway [{ref:pathway-androgen-biosynthesis}]. One of its two member genes in the knowledge base is associated with PCOS, the strongest being CYP17A1 [{ref:pathway-androgen-biosynthesis}].
Flutamide is a nonsteroidal antiandrogen [{ref:therapeutic-flutamide}]. The knowledge base does not cover hepatotoxicity.
Testosterone is an androstanoid with 17beta-hydroxy and 3-oxo groups, and it has a role as an androgen [{ref:hormone-testosterone}].
Letrozole blocks the active site of CYP19A1, which prevents the conversion of androgens to estrogen [{ref:therapeutic-letrozole}].
